task.title: runBinary calls t.Fatalf from a worker goroutine and reports the failed process as a clean exit 0
task.description:
internal/cli/multiprocess_test.go:239 (the `default` branch of `runBinary`), reached from the goroutines `runConcurrently` starts at multiprocess_test.go:208-213. Added in PR #33 (commit 29c8daa).

`testing.T.Fatalf` may only be called from the goroutine running the test function. Called from a worker it runs `runtime.Goexit`, which skips the assignment to `outcomes[index]`, runs the deferred `group.Done()`, and lets `group.Wait()` return normally. The slot is left as the zero value `processOutcome{code: 0, stdout: "", stderr: ""}`, so the test reads a process that never ran as a successful exit 0.

Failure scenario: the built binary is missing or not executable - a partially written temp dir, a noexec /tmp, ETXTBSY on a slow filesystem - so `command.Run()` returns something that is not an *exec.ExitError. The create loop then takes the `outcome.code == 0` branch and calls `decodeMutationTask` on an empty stdout, and the test dies with "decode create task: unexpected end of JSON input" instead of naming the real cause. The diagnostic points at JSON decoding when the actual problem is that the binary could not be executed.

Fix: give `processOutcome` an `err` field, have `runBinary` record the error and return instead of calling t.Fatalf, and fail from the main goroutine after `group.Wait()` when any outcome carries one. `mustRunBinary` and the direct (non-concurrent) callers can keep failing immediately, since they already run on the test goroutine.

Deferred from PR #33: it only changes the diagnostic on a failure path that has not fired, and the PR was scoped to the two major review findings.
